question: In the 1990s France extended housing benefit to many more renters. Of each extra euro of benefit, how much went into higher rents?
answer: Most of it. Gabrielle Fack estimated that between 50 and 80 cents of each extra euro ended up as higher rent for low-income tenants. Flats barely grew in number while the reform drew students into renting alone. A subsidy to buyers in a market that cannot expand ends up with the sellers.
move: Before subsidising buyers, ask whether sellers can make any more.
trap: Assuming the benefit stays with the tenant it is paid to.

diagram.caption: Of each extra euro of benefit, 50 to 80 cents went on higher rents.

reference: Fack, Are housing benefit an effective way to redistribute income? Evidence from a natural experiment in France, Labour Economics, 2006
